tools/wall_channel_census.py:1464 -- two of the three versioned seams (interface/contracts/flex_observable_seam.py, interface/contracts/payment_observable_seam.py) run request=dormant: they declare a request leg this build never sends, so the company receives their observations as responses to nothing. That is the reviewer's named fail shape, 'we model it as a response to a synthetic request', predicted before any code was seen. Pass 34 gave the census a question that REDS on it; the seam itself is unrepaired.

interface/contracts/wall_envelope.py -- correlation_id links exactly one request to one response; four functions, no multi-leg conversation exists. No DCC request/ack/response/alert and no switch-with-objection can be expressed.

WallStatus.TIMEOUT has neither a reader nor a writer -- company/billing/payment_observation_consumer.py and company/market/flex_participation.py:270 both collapse non-OK, and pass 35's vocabulary count found no writer either. No 1-minute / 24-hour / 5-working-day horizon ladder exists at all. Pass 36 gave NOT_KNOWABLE_YET a reader (liveness 1/4 -> 2/4), which is a different member of the same vocabulary.

The seam REFUSES spec-violating input (tests/company/interfaces/test_wall_protocol.py:219, :673) and the consumer handles duplicates and out-of-order revisions (tests/company/billing/test_payment_observation_consumer.py:383, :769 -- C-S1/C-S2). What does not exist is the reviewer's actual subject: a STAND-IN capable of EMITTING spec-violating traffic -- duplicate flow references, readings for unsupplied MPANs, backlog bursts -- used in regression. The malformed inputs are hand-built test fixtures, not counterparty behaviour.

No contract tests run against any counterparty's real test environment, and none can: tools/company_network_isolation.py makes it a WALL that company/ and saas/ may not open a socket, ever, directly or transitively. Divergence between stand-in and real counterparty is therefore undetectable by construction in this epoch. Lifting it means contacting real organisations (reserved class 2); EP19_counterparty_qualification_paths (epoch 5) holds the register and its own ceiling is the register, never the application.

company/interfaces/wall_protocol.py:91 -- SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS: frozenset[int] = frozenset({1}). A single GLOBAL version constant with no per-counterparty dimension, which is exactly the shape the reviewer said means every market release is a big-bang cutover. Two versions of one interface cannot run concurrently.

company/interfaces/wall_protocol.py:176-179 -- a version outside SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS raises UNSUPPORTED_VERSION and an absent one raises MISSING_FIELD, so the stamp is ENFORCED on receipt rather than carried. The module's docstring (line 43) names the sibling FAIL-OPEN it exists to avoid: tools/*_port.py's entry.get('schema_version', SCHEMA_VERSION), a decoder supplying the answer it is checking.

There is NO counterparty authentication anywhere below the port. A repo-wide search for SMKI, DIP signing, DTN participant identity, mutual TLS or client certificates returns hits only in background/one_way_door.py:196 and tests/background/test_one_way_door.py:323 -- i.e. the project models SMKI accession solely as a RESERVED REAL-WORLD ACT, never as a verified property of a message. This is the reviewer's precise objection: indistinguishability from a stand-in was achieved by the identity check being absent from the path, which is a control gap and not an abstraction. Modelling identity verification below the port against a stand-in needs no real certificate, so this is ordinary build work and is NOT epoch-gated.

Nothing stops a stand-in configuration reaching production because nothing distinguishes them: no environment segregation and no startup assertion exists across interface/contracts/, company/interfaces/, simulation/payment_seam_adapter.py or sim/flex_dispatch.py. The network-isolation wall makes the question moot TODAY (the company has no route out at all), but the reviewer's subject is the go-live seam, which is what this atom claims to be.

Nothing runs against DCC SIT/UIT/UEPT, CSS test or the DIP test environments -- a repo-wide search finds no such target -- and this layer feeds no Elexon qualification or REC entry-assessment evidence. Same wall as Q9: reaching those systems means contacting real organisations and spending real money (reserved classes 1 and 2). EP19_counterparty_qualification_paths (epoch 5) is where that register lives.

The honest 'they don't, they're outside this' -- which the reviewer explicitly named as fine and expected, and warned that claiming they fit is the tell of a description generalised from the settlement side. A streaming price feed is channel F (published artefact, company/interfaces/market_feed_publication.py:11), not the two-legged channel-C envelope; a gate-closure-critical ECVN submission is not modelled at all and appears only as a reserved real-world act (tests/background/test_one_way_door.py:333, 'accede to the Balancing and Settlement Code and appoint an ECVN agent'). Neither is claimed to fit the async model.
